answer.rationale: With the contract expiring in 14 days and the line running at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, switching primary vendors now carries onboarding and ramp risk that could interrupt deliveries just as capacity is tightest — a risk the consolidated memory_c2 summary (fast onboarding, accurate invoicing) doesn't address at all regarding delivery reliability or lead-time performance under load. I verified memory_c2's archived source to check for any noted delivery/quality caveats before ruling out the switch. Given the mandate is a cost cut, not necessarily lowest-price-at-any-cost, and memory_c4 shows renegotiation with the incumbent has recovered real margin (price and terms) without migration risk or delivery interruption, and memory_c1 shows incumbent renewals preserve integration stability, negotiating terms with the incumbent is the lower-risk path to meaningful savings this cycle. This doesn't fully resolve the 18% target the way switching would, so I'm flagging that a full vendor-switch cost/risk tradeoff still needs deeper evaluation next cycle rather than assuming the low-cost quote is safe at current capacity. Scale is kept small/guarded since this is a one-time renegotiation of the primary contract, not a rollout across other lines or components.
